sites.operation: STG.E [R6.64], R23 (st.global.f32, SASS 0x1890; executed only by threadIdx.x == 0 after the block reduction)

LDG.E (gradInput_k[i], ld.global.f32) + LDG.E (*gradOutput_k) + STG.E (gradInput_k[i], st.global.f32); the loop is unrolled in the SASS (copies at 0x1ab0..0x1d30 in the buggy driver, load/store of gradInput_k[i] at e.g. 0x1ac0/0x1b30)

thread_pair_example: driver input: 1 frame, dim = 128, target = 64, launch <<<1, 128>>> (block 0): thread 0 (warp 0) stores gradInput_k[64] at L121; thread 64 (warp 2, threadIdx.x == target_k % 128; its single iteration i = 64 of the L124 loop, because i_start = 64, i_step = 128) loads gradInput_k[64], multiplies by *gradOutput_k and stores it at L125. The two touch the same global word with no barrier between them. (Benign only if target_k % 128 == 0: then thread 0 owns the slot itself.)
class_reason: Both accesses are plain (non-volatile, non-atomic) global float accesses to one word, issued by threads of different warps of the same block with no happens-before edge: the last __syncthreads in the buggy kernel is at L113, before the reduction that produces the L121 store, and nothing orders thread 0's L121 store with the other threads' L125 loop. No strong/atomic access is involved, so DR (not SC) under D20. Note: the tool-level report may be raced as WAW (L121 store vs L125 store) and RAW/WAR (L121 store vs L125 load); all are the same pair of source lines and the same word.
buggy_expected: the pair L121 STG (thread 0) x L125 LDG/STG (thread target_k % 128) on global gradInput_k[target_k] is reported as DR (global-memory race, cross-warp same block)

fixed.reason: the fix inserts one __syncthreads() at fixed L124, between the thread-0-only block (L116-L122) and the scaling loop (now fixed L125-L127, RMW at fixed L126): the barrier orders thread 0's L121 store before every thread's RMW. verify.expected_report_fixed: nothing for that pair. The other gradInput_k[i] writes (L107, L109) are by the owning thread i and are ordered before the L121 / RMW accesses by the existing barrier at L113 (and each element has a single writer).
